# disnan

> Tests whether a double-precision floating-point number is NaN.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import disnan from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/disnan';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
disnan( din ) → boolean
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `din` | `number` | Value to test |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `din`: Input to test for NaN.

</details>

**Returns** `boolean`: result

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
disnan.ndarray( din ) → boolean
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `din` | `number` | Value to test |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `din`: Input to test for NaN.

</details>

**Returns** `boolean`: true if NaN, false otherwise

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `disnan()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DISNAN`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/disnan.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import disnan from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/disnan';

// Using the standard interface:
let out = disnan( 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = disnan.ndarray( 1 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DISNAN`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DISNAN returns .TRUE. if its argument is NaN, and .FALSE. otherwise. To be replaced by the Fortran 2003 intrinsic in the future.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
